rationale: Flutter/bloc coverage for the dart lane, which had none. MEASURED 2026-10-07 with `bun validation/m14/fixtures/dart/dump-symbols.mts`: the first version of this expectation asserted `uses` for the two type-argument edges and a bare `build` for the override target, and it FAILED on all three. The dump shows the analyzer was already right and the EXPECTATION was wrong: a type mention is published as `references` at 0.95 (real-dart-analyzer.ts collectTypeMention), and an `overrides` target is owner-qualified (`StatelessWidget.build`). Recorded rather than quietly corrected, because a fixture whose expectations are written from assumption instead of measurement manufactures defects that do not exist - which is what happened here, for three cells, on the first run. The claims now pinned: the bloc/cubit dependency written inside angle brackets IS an edge whose target is the type argument, in both call shapes; the generic static `BlocBase.of<T>()` resolves the same way; `with X` is a mixin application and publishes `uses`; and an in-file framework base is a real target for `extends` and for `overrides`. The framework types are DECLARED IN THE FIXTURE on purpose so this measures the ANALYZER and not the corpus: a real Flutter corpus does not contain packages/flutter (0 files for lib/src/widgets), and that separate population gap is recorded in docs/analyzers/LAPTOP-B-STATUS.md.

expectRelationships.comment: THE CLAIM: `context.read<CounterCubit>()` names CounterCubit inside the angle brackets, and the edge target IS that type argument (not the method `read`). A type mention is `references`, not `uses`.
THE CLAIM, second shape: `BlocBase.of<CounterBloc>(context)` - the BlocProvider.of<T>() pattern - resolves the same way.
the call itself is labelled separately, so the type argument is not double-counted as a use of `read`
the return type of build() is a type position
the parameter type of build() is a type position
plain Dart: a bloc extends Cubit<T>
plain Dart: a widget extends its framework base
`with X` is a mixin application; 2026-10-18 it records `mixes_in`, not `uses`
an override target is OWNER-QUALIFIED: the member it replaces, not the bare name
a getter override of an inherited framework member

forbidRelationships.comment: the `on BuildContext` clause of an EXTENSION is not the widget's base
the bloc dependency must be `references` (a type mention), not `uses` - pinning the label so it cannot drift to the weaker edge
